title: DNS/DHCP Incident Triage
subject: DNS + DHCP
description: Practice triage → diagnosis → fix workflows in a realistic ticket queue.
reportOverview: This activity simulates common DNS/DHCP operational incidents. Work each ticket through triage, diagnosis, and fix, then document your change note. After resolution, review the debrief to reinforce the troubleshooting approach.

tickets.title: Users can’t resolve internal hostnames
tickets.summary: Multiple workstations report intermittent DNS lookup failures for internal domains.
artifact: Affected users are in multiple subnets

triage.q: What is the best first triage step?
options: Verify scope and impact across users/subnets
Flush DNS cache on all endpoints

diagnosis.q: What evidence most strongly points to the likely cause?
options: Clients can’t ping the DNS server
DNS client timeouts with server reachable
Update DNS forwarder configuration and validate recursion

validations: Run nslookup intranet.newvue.local from two different subnets
Resolve at least 10 internal records successfully
Check DNS server logs for new errors after the change

debrief.title: Resolution Summary
debrief.summary: The incident looked like a client-side DNS failure, but network reachability to the DNS server was healthy. By confirming impact first and then validating the resolution path, we isolated the failure to upstream recursion and corrected the forwarder configuration.
whatGoodLooksLike: Confirm scope and blast radius before making changes.
Separate connectivity problems from DNS resolution-path problems.
Make one controlled change, then re-test from multiple vantage points.
validation: Verify resolution from multiple subnets and at least one known-good test host.
Repeat lookups several times to confirm stability (not a one-off success).
Review DNS logs to ensure errors stop after the change.
debrief.takeaway: Triage scope first, then validate the resolution chain end-to-end.
